body:
`CumulativeGammaDistribution` limits its series and continued fraction to 100 iterations without exposing a budget. On `84fbf0a0e`, ordinary finite inputs such as gamma shape 500 at x = 500 throw "too few iterations". Central chi-square inherits the failure through its gamma-CDF call.

Return `boost::math::gamma_p`, already used elsewhere in QuantLib, while keeping the `x <= 0` guard and constructor validation.

| Call | `84fbf0a0e` | This PR | mpmath reference |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Gamma shape 500, x = 500 | throws | 0.50594714617076031 | 0.50594714617076036 |
| Chi-square df = 1000, x = 1000 | throws | 0.50594714617076031 | 0.50594714617076036 |

`testCumulativeGammaDistributionLargeShapes` adds 19 reference cases; `testCumulativeChiSquareDistributionLargeDegreesOfFreedom` adds seven. References use mpmath 1.3.0 at 60 digits, checked at 1e-12 relative tolerance, covering moderate and large parameters and both sides of the distribution. Against `84fbf0a0e`, 22 rows fail, including eight exceptions; four upper-side controls pass.

Boost's numerical and error policies now apply after the guard. In throwaway probes with Boost 1.83.0, gamma shape 1 returned 1 at +infinity and NaN at a NaN argument; chi-square with infinite degrees of freedom returned NaN at x = 2. These previously threw. Gamma at a = x = 1e15 still threw, now a Boost exception rather than `QuantLib::Error`.

A throwaway single-thread benchmark at seven inputs measured approximately 0.24–1.2 microseconds per call, versus 0.07–0.34 previously. Poisson, binomial, non-central chi-square and the explicitly budgeted incomplete functions are unchanged.

Implementation validation on Ubuntu 24.04 with g++ 13.3.0, Boost 1.83.0, Release and warnings as errors: all 38 cases in `FunctionsTests` and `DistributionTests` pass in C++17 and C++20. MSVC, Clang, AAD, other Boost versions and the full suite were not run.

    ./build/test-suite/quantlib-test-suite --run_test=QuantLibTests/FunctionsTests:QuantLibTests/DistributionTests --log_level=message

title: Fix the gamma and chi-square CDFs for large parameters
